correctness.rationale: For b,q>0 and h>=0 the symmetric part of the drift is negative definite, so the unit-diffusion Lyapunov solution exists and is positive definite. Eliminating the three diagonal entries first, I independently solved a 3-by-3 system for the off-diagonal entries and verified the covariance equation. The Lyapunov identities give V=3-h S11 and tr(S^-1)=-tr(M); the all-even current integral then reduces to tr(M S M^T)+tr(M), without covariance inversion. This reproduces the rational EPR, its factored derivative, the minimum and endpoints, and all variance derivative numerator coefficients. The independent exact check is replayable with Python 3 and SymPy at /workspace/review_evidence/check_5.py. For B=b^2<=1 the variance derivative numerator T is strictly positive (c4 may be zero); for B>1 its leading coefficient is negative and c0,c1 are positive. The only problematic c2<=0 requires Q=q^2<1 and B>25, forcing c3<0, so there is exactly one sign change in every case with B>1. Descartes plus the opposite endpoint signs gives the unique positive root and minimum. For q=2 the first EPR derivative factor becomes a positive constant, not zero; for q>2 only this factor crosses once at the claimed h. The limiting values are 2 and 2q^2. Scope is the stated isotropic all-even OU family, not a parity-independent thermodynamic result.

evidence: Kharbanda–Burnet–Sabass give the residual EPR mechanism, directional approach and a four-dimensional example. Godrèche–Luck give multivariate OU steady-state methods and a three-site asymmetric Gaussian chain.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Asymptotic residual-current theory does not establish global uniqueness or all four regimes, and the three-site Gaussian spin-chain drift is not the one-parameter extra-damping skew chain.

evidence: Existing methods compute stationary covariance/EPR and explain approaches to the strong-coupling residual. The closest exact reversal theorem treats the separate feedback drift.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The limiting mechanism and general Gaussian formulas are inputs, but they do not mechanically supply the independent global thresholds: in particular the variance numerator can have mixed coefficient signs, and uniqueness requires excluding multiple positive roots throughout the parameter domain.

evidence: The feedback record gives the unique EPR minimum at k*=(5−2h)/(2(h−1)) for 1<h<5/2. Its damped-to-residual cross block in the symmetric part of its printed drift is nonzero; the skew chain's corresponding block is zero.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An orthogonal change of coordinates preserving unit diffusion and carrying the rank-one damping projector to the new damped axis preserves whether this cross block vanishes. Thus the feedback theorem is not this family in different orthonormal coordinates, even allowing parameter rescaling. It also gives no variance threshold.

value.rationale: This natural small driven chain disentangles response of a fluctuation measure from that of stationary current, without changing diffusion normalization or stability. Its exact dividing lines and unique-minimum theorem realize all four regimes while varying independent couplings, strengthening the general observation that dissipation can rise toward its residual limit. The variance sign/uniqueness result is the substantive extra constraint, not mere evaluation of a stationary Gaussian formula.
residual_risks: Value is model-specific and does not imply a general thermodynamic relation between total variance and entropy production.
